$comment: TEMPLATE — COPY, DO NOT EDIT IN PLACE.
cp appsettings.Development.template.json appsettings.Development.json
appsettings.Development.json is git-ignored. This template is committed so a new
contributor can see EVERY key the service reads, with an explanation of each.
SECRETS DO NOT BELONG IN THE FILE YOU CREATE EITHER. Even git-ignored, a secret in a
working-tree file leaks through backups, editor histories, container build contexts and
the occasional `git add -f`. Use user-secrets, which live outside the repository:
dotnet user-secrets set "Database:ConnectionString" "<value>" \
--project src/SchoolManagement.Api
Every value below is empty or a safe non-secret default, on purpose. There are no
realistic-looking placeholder credentials here: a fake password that looks real is the
thing that gets copied into a deployment and then quietly works until it does not.

MinimumLevel.$comment: Debug locally to see the pipeline behaviours' output. Information in deployment.

Override.$comment_ef: Set to Information to see every SQL statement EF Core executes.

$comment_connection: REQUIRED, AND A SECRET — set it with user-secrets, not here. Startup fails without it.
Need a local PostgreSQL? See README.md, 'Running a local database'.
$comment_sensitive: EnableSensitiveDataLogging writes query PARAMETER VALUES into logs — that is user data.
Useful when debugging a query locally; the app REFUSES TO START with it enabled outside
Development. Leave it false unless you are actively debugging.

$comment: 'Placeholder' authenticates NOBODY: anonymous endpoints work, protected ones return 401.
That is the intended local state until the identity provider is chosen — a decision that
needs human sign-off (root CLAUDE.md §5). Tracked in docs/ASSUMPTIONS.md.
Add the local frontend's origin here, exactly — scheme + host + port, no trailing slash.
Vite's default is http://localhost:5173. Wildcards are REJECTED at startup.
AllowCredentials must match the frontend's fetch `credentials` mode or every cross-origin
call fails in a way that looks like a CORS bug.

RateLimiting.$comment: Raised locally so exploratory clicking does not trip the limiter.

RequestLimits.$comment: 1 MiB body cap, 32 levels of JSON nesting.

$comment: Leave OtlpEndpoint EMPTY unless a collector is actually running — exporting to nothing
produces a constant stream of connection errors that hides the logs you want to read.
With a local collector, it is usually http://localhost:4317.

Pipeline.$comment: Lower this locally to find slow requests earlier; it only controls a log warning.
